title: Endpoint kernel and cokernel forks for the strict vertical cutoff comparison
statement: Let $C$ be abelian, $L$ a cochain complex indexed by $\mathbb N$, and $0<a<b$ integers. Define $T_c$ by [lem-sp-double-complex-vertical-tower-maps] and $W[a,b)$ by [def-sp-double-complex-vertical-window]. Let $g:T_a(L)\to T_b(L)$ satisfy $g\iota_b=\iota_a$. Put $m=a.\mathrm{toNat}-1$, $n=a.\mathrm{toNat}$, $B=T_b(L)$, $E=L$ extended by zero to $\mathbb Z$, and $r:T_b(L)\to W[a,b)(L)$ equal to the restriction of $\tau_{\le b-1}(E\to\tau_{\ge a}E)$. Then $g^m$ exhibits $T_a(L)^m$ as the kernel of $d_B^{m,n}$, and $r^n$ exhibits $W[a,b)(L)^n$ as the cokernel of $d_B^{m,n}$. In particular both required zero-composite equations hold. No assertion about $\ker q$ is assumed or included.

source.place: homology-section-truncations, cochain canonical truncations (3) and (4), specialized to the boundary of the upper cutoff.

proof.text: Use the cochain truncation formulas of Tag 0118. Write E for L extended by zero and B for its upper cutoff at b-1. In degree a-1, the inclusion B -> E is invertible because a-1 < b-1; in degree a it is monomorphic. The lower cutoff at a-1 identifies its boundary object with cycles of E at a-1, hence with the kernel of E.d(a-1,a). The factorization equation hg identifies g with that cycles inclusion into B. Transport the cycles kernel fork through the degree-(a-1) isomorphism; postcomposition of B.d with the monomorphic inclusion at a detects its zero composites, giving the first kernel fork.

If a < b-1, both B and E agree at a. The lower projection at a is E.pOpcycles a, which is the cokernel of E.d(a-1,a). Upper truncation does not change this coordinate, so transport E.opcyclesIsCokernel along the truncation coordinate isomorphisms. If a=b-1, B at a is E.cycles a. In this case the window coordinate is E.homology a: taking cycles of the lower truncation at a computes cycles modulo the preceding image. The map is E.homologyπ a, which is the cokernel of E.toCycles(a-1,a). The differential of B into its cycles boundary is exactly that toCycles map after the invertible degree-(a-1) inclusion. Transport E.homologyIsCokernel to obtain the second fork.

The component zero-composite equations follow from the two forks, or from the chain-map identities and the zero degree-a term of the lower cutoff and zero degree-(a-1) term of the window. Since a>0, restriction keeps both integer boundary degrees, which become a.toNat-1 and a.toNat. This includes a=1, adjacent endpoints b=a+1, the zero complex, and zero differentials.

theorem verticalCutoff_endpoint_forks
    (L : CochainComplex C ℕ) (a b : ℤ) (hab : a < b) (ha : 0 < a)
    (g : (verticalCutoff a).obj L ⟶ (verticalCutoff b).obj L)
    (hg : g ≫ (verticalCutoffι b).app L = (verticalCutoffι a).app L) :
    (∃ h : g.f (a.toNat - 1) ≫
        ((verticalCutoff b).obj L).d (a.toNat - 1) a.toNat = 0,
      Nonempty (IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι (g.f (a.toNat - 1)) h))) ∧
    (∃ h : ((verticalCutoff b).obj L).d (a.toNat - 1) a.toNat ≫
        (HomologicalComplex.restrictionMap
          (CochainComplex.truncLEMap
            (CochainComplex.πTruncGE (L.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) a) (b - 1))
          ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat).f a.toNat = 0,
      Nonempty (IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ
        ((HomologicalComplex.restrictionMap
          (CochainComplex.truncLEMap
            (CochainComplex.πTruncGE (L.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) a) (b - 1))
          ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat).f a.toNat) h)))
